values.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
values.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
values.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

values.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
values.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
values.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

values.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
values.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
values.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.

values.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

values.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
values.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
values.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.

values.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
values.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
values.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.

While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
values.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
values.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.

values.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

values.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
values.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
values.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.

values.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

values.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
values.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.
values.4: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.

values.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

values.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
values.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
values.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.

values.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
values.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
values.4: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

values.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
values.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
values.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.

values.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

values.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
values.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
values.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.

values.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
values.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
values.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.

However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.

Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
values.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

values.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
values.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
values.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.

Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.

Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
values.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. values.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.

The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.

The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.

His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.

values.seasonOutlook: Due to a variety of injuries, Lloyd has appeared in one game since being selected in the third round of the 2024 draft. Now healthy, he appears to have a hold on No. 2 RB duties in Green Bay, which is notable with Josh Jacobs facing a potential suspension. Lloyd is likely to open the season on the RB2/flex radar and should be on your radar in the middle rounds, though note that he'll fade back to no more than an insurance stash once Jacobs returns.

One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. values.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.

Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.

values.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.

After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
values.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.

values.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.
values.3: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.
values.4: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.

values.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

values.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
values.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
values.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.

Love was largely held in check by the Chargers in Week 1, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and catching two passes for nine yards, but he did get into the end zone on a five-yard run. He logged six fewer carries and 20 fewer rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier, which isn't ideal for fantasy managers who drafted the rookie with the expectation that he'd be the lead back right off the bat. Even if Love gets a larger share of the workload against Seattle, he could struggle against a defense that held Patriots No. 1 RB Rhamondre Stevenson to 2.8 YPC in a Week 1 win.

Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.
values.4: Jeremiyah Love appears to have ascended to the clear-cut No. 1 RB in Arizona heading into a Week 4 clash versus the Giants. Love handled a career-high 26 touches (21 carries and five catches) this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, compiling 90 yards on the ground and 19 (along with a TD) through the air. Tyler Allgeier was the only other Cardinals RB to log a carry in the contest, and he got just two totes. There could be room for Love to run against the Giants, who are giving up 5.05 yards per carry to running backs, the third-worst mark in the league through three weeks.

values.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
values.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.
values.4: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.

values.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

values.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
values.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
values.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.

Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
values.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
values.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

values.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
values.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
values.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.

values.seasonOutlook: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

Reed struggled even with seven targets in a loss to the Vikings, logging just three catches for 20 yards. The fourth-year playmaker could start to slip into a WR3 role if he continues to play similarly, but luckily there appears to be plenty of targets to go around in the short term. Reed will face a New York defense that ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers this past Sunday.
values.3: Jayden Reed's status is up in the air as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Reed was carted off the field after injuring his back on the first drive of Week 2, which in itself makes it unlikely that he'll be rushed back for a TNF matchup. The fourth-year playmaker's absence would give Matthew Golden even more looks, with Skyy Moore and Bo Melton slotting in as supplementary options for Jordan Love. If Reed somehow does play, he'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.

The fourth-year wide receiver also has no current return timeline. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.

Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
values.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

values.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
values.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
values.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
values.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
values.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

values.seasonOutlook: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.

values.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.

Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.

Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. values.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

values.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

values.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

(Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.
